info.name: Egoola API — Category
info.description:
Category reference data (Admin-only) — the single unified tree used for both product and service listings. No Retrieve (405) — only List, Create, Update, Delete. `slug` is always server-generated from `name`, and duplicate names are checked per `type` — the same name is fine once under `product` and once under `service`, but not twice within the same type.

`parent` is optional and nullable — a category can be created or moved under another category later, or detached back to top-level. Two rules are enforced server-side: a parent must be the *same type* as its child (a product category can't sit under a service category, or vice versa), and no chain of parents may loop back on itself (directly — B can't be A's parent when A is already B's parent — or through a deeper nested chain).

How to use:
1. Pick the `Egoola - Local` environment (or edit `base_url`).
2. Run **Auth > Admin Login** first — its "Tests" script saves the access/refresh tokens into collection variables automatically.
3. Run **Categories > Create Parent Category** — its "Tests" script saves the new row's id into `category_id`.
4. Run **Categories > Create Child Category** — it sends `{{category_id}}` as `parent`, and saves its own id into `child_category_id`.
5. The three Update requests below show attaching, moving, and removing a parent on an already-existing category.
6. When a 401 says the token expired, run **Auth > Refresh Token**.

For login/Admin/Seller/Buyer management, see the separate Egoola API — Accounts & Auth collection. For Country/State/City/Thana, see the separate Egoola API — Geography collection.

request.description: Public endpoint — no token needed to call this. Returns access + refresh JWTs carrying actor_type=admin. Every Catalog endpoint below is Admin-only.
Exchanges the saved refresh token (14-day life) for a new access token (1-hour life). Run this instead of logging in again once the access token expires.

`type` and `name` required; `parent` is left out here, so this lands as a top-level category. `slug` is always server-generated from `name` and checked for duplicates within the same `type` only — the same name is fine under the other type. `image`/`sort_order`/`status` are optional — send `image` only when actually attaching a file (multipart), or drop the whole form-data body and send plain JSON with just `type`/`name` when there's no image.

`parent` must be the id of a category of the *same* `type` — pointing it at a category of the other type returns a 400 on the `parent` field. There's no depth limit; a child can itself be used as a parent for a grandchild, and so on.

Any subset of type/name/image/sort_order/status. Renaming regenerates slug and re-checks it for duplicates (within the same type). To replace the image, send a multipart request with a new `image` file instead of this raw JSON body.

Works the same whether the category previously had no parent at all, or already had a different one — this just overwrites whatever `parent` currently is. Rejected with a 400 if `parent`'s type doesn't match this category's type, or if it would create a cycle (this category, directly or through a nested chain, is already an ancestor of the given parent).

item.name: Update Category — move to a different parent

request.description: Same request shape as attaching a parent — send the new parent's id and it replaces the old one. Edit the raw body above to point at a different category id to see it actually move.

Explicit `null` detaches the category back to top-level. Omitting `parent` from the body entirely (rather than sending null) leaves whatever parent is already set untouched — that's how the other PATCH requests in this collection avoid accidentally clearing it.
